chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Mansur ibn Yunus and Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him saying: 'The earth cannot be devoid [of an Imam] except that there would be an Imam in it, so that if the believers exceed in something, he would bring them back, and if they fall short in something, he would complete it for them.'

key_terms.إمام: Imam — the divinely-appointed, infallible religious and political authority from the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.الأرض: The earth/world — used here to mean the inhabited world at any given moment in time
key_terms.زاد: To exceed/go beyond proper limits — referring to believers who add to or distort religious practice
key_terms.كيما: In order that/so that — particle indicating the teleological purpose of the Imam's perpetual presence
key_terms.نقص: To fall short/be deficient — referring to believers who omit obligations or fail in religious duty

ai.seo_question: Does the earth always have a living Imam according to Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms the doctrine of continuous Imamate — that the earth is never without a living Imam at any moment in history. This teaching responds to the theological need for a divinely-guided authority who corrects believers when they go astray and supplements their understanding when they fall short. In early Shia thought, this was foundational proof for the indispensability of the Imam as the guardian of religious practice and doctrine.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Muhammad Bin Abu Umeyr, from Mansour Bin Yunus and Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The earth cannot be empty except there would be an Imam<sup>asws</sup> so that if the Momineen exceed in something, he<sup>asws</sup> would return them, and if they are deficient in something, he<sup>asws</sup> would complete it for them’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Muhammad ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mansur ibn Yunus and Su‘dan ibn Muslim from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammara from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following. “

I heard the Imam (a.s.) saying, ‘The earth is never left without an Imam so that if the believers would add any thing it would be brought back and if they would reduce anything it would be completed.”
